newsitem.title: MEXICO: Bombscare at hospital where Mexican druglord died.
newsitem.headline: Bombscare at hospital where Mexican druglord died.

text.p: A Mexican hospital where notorious drug kingpin Amado Carrillo Fuentes was believed to have died after having surgery last week was evacuated late on Monday because of a bomb threat, police said.
Police inspector Hector Gaytan said a caller telephoned the hospital and warned of a bomb, forcing the evacuation of doctors, nurses and some patients.
But police later combed the building and found no trace of explosives, he said.

The Santa Monica hospital in the up-scale Polanco district of Mexico City was thrust into the spotlight over the weekend, when it emerged that Carrillo, Mexico's most wanted drug lord, died there of a heart attack after undergoing plastic surgery and liposuction.

Carrillo apparently entered the hospital under a fake name. The decomposing body, which has been positively identified by U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) officials -- though Mexican authorities have still confirmed the identification -- was displayed to hordes of photographers in Mexico City on Monday.

Carrillo, head of the Juarez Cartel, was known as "Lord of the Skies" for the cargoes of cocaine he flew to Mexico from Colombia for shipment to the United States. He had been described by the DEA as "the most powerful figure in the Mexican drug trade."
